summary: Live combat converges on one attack pipeline (attacks.js rollAttack, SWSERoll.rollAttack delegates) and one damage-application boundary (ActorEngine.applyDamage -> DamageResolutionEngine). Of the multi-domain leads only the house-rule damage threshold is a confirmed live duplicate (DerivedCalculator vs ThresholdEngine, different formulas — rules/owner question). Other competing calculators (defense, crit multiplier/range, damage formula, CT penalty, CombatEngine.applyDamage) sit on unreferenced entry points, uncalled locals or wrappers. Confirmed live defects: Combat Action Browser calls a non-existent SWSECombat.runCombatAction; combat bookkeeping flags are written directly (A-02) including mid-resolution in DamageResolutionEngine; combat-ui-behavior-hotfix remains a parallel execution path with a chat monkey-patch (A-09).

findings.title: Combat bookkeeping flags written with raw setFlag/unsetFlag, incl. mid-resolution in DamageResolutionEngine
findings.observed: Actor-owned flags (encounter-use counters, stay-up, quick-comeback, threshold-exceeded, emergency patch, action-economy turn state, combat status, pinned actions) are written with actor.setFlag/unsetFlag although ActorEngine.updateActorFlags/unsetActorFlag exist. DamageResolutionEngine.resolveDamage writes them during resolution, before ActorEngine.applyDamage persists HP/CT, so a later failure leaves bookkeeping without damage. Other P-A02 sites in the domain are legitimate: SWSEInitiative Combatant writes (Foundry world docs), poison-engine:126/273 and fire-state-store:292 (world-item fallbacks; fire-state lacks the @mutation-exception comment), attacks.js:1402 (false positive, service call), active-effects-manager.js:61 (token document; legacy token effects array, F-CMB-010 follow-up).
findings.proposedSolution: Return bookkeeping deltas from resolveDamage and persist them in ActorEngine.applyDamage's single update; route other flag writes through ActorEngine.updateActorFlags. Add @mutation-exception comments on the Combatant and world-item writes.
findings.alternatives: Keep flags but move writes after applyDamage commits.
findings.regressionTests: Failure injection after resolveDamage: no flag changed. Probe P-A02 ratchet for combat.
findings.foundryAcceptance: Stay-up / quick-comeback / threshold-first-exceedance in live combat.
findings.simplificationBenefit: One write per damage event; fewer re-renders.

findings.title: CombatEngine.applyDamage is a second, incomplete damage writer with no caller
findings.observed: Calls DamageResolutionEngine.resolveDamage then writes only system.hp.value and conditionTrack.current via ActorEngine.updateActor (no bonus/temp HP, shields, persistent CT, droid states, FP-rescue receipt that ActorEngine.applyDamage handles). No static caller, not in packs, CombatEngine not global.
findings.proposedSolution: Delete the method or make it delegate to ActorEngine.applyDamage (legacy C/D).
findings.regressionTests: architecture-combat-authority guard: no second resolveDamage caller.

findings.title: House-rule damage threshold computed independently by DerivedCalculator and ThresholdEngine with different formulas
findings.observed: RAW mode: ThresholdEngine reads system.derived.damageThreshold (single authority). With enableEnhancedMassiveDamage+modifyDamageThresholdFormula, DerivedCalculator stores base(incl. size, feat Will-base, flat/modifier adjustments)+level+size again, while ThresholdEngine.calculateDamageThreshold (used by evaluateThreshold on the live ActorEngine.applyDamage path) returns fort+level+size, ignoring the adjustments. Displayed DT and the DT used for the CT check differ under the house rule.
findings.intendedOwnership: DerivedCalculator owns DT (A-03); ThresholdEngine reads it.
findings.proposedSolution: After the owner rules on the house-rule formula, compute it once in DerivedCalculator and have calculateDamageThreshold always read system.derived.damageThreshold.
findings.alternatives: ThresholdEngine owns the house-rule formula and DerivedCalculator calls it.
findings.regressionTests: With the house rule on, derived DT === ThresholdEngine DT for character/droid/vehicle fixtures.
findings.foundryAcceptance: House rule enabled live; sheet DT equals applied threshold.
findings.risk: Changes house-rule outcomes — needs ruling first.

findings.title: Live Combat Action Browser executes SWSECombat.runCombatAction, which does not exist
findings.observed: SWSECombatActionBrowser is initialized at init and opened from sidebar/Token HUD; _executeAction calls SWSECombat.runCombatAction. SWSECombat defines no such method; the only assignment is in the never-registered aid-another adapter. Clicking an action throws a TypeError. OSI lists the old combat action browser as a retirement candidate.
findings.proposedSolution: Owner decision: retire the browser (remove init + Token HUD button; legacy B) or route execution to the combat-feature action router.
findings.alternatives: Temporary guard that disables execution with a notice.
findings.regressionTests: Test that every init-registered UI action resolves to a defined handler.
findings.foundryAcceptance: Click an action in the browser live.

findings.title: SWSERoll.rollAutofire / rollFullAttack keep independent defense, crit-range and crit-multiplier math; no in-repo caller
findings.observed: These entry points read target.system.defenses.reflex.total ?? 10 (no derived defense, Command Cover or observation bonus), use getEffectiveCritRange (EXTEND_CRITICAL_RANGE) instead of CombatOptionResolver criticalThreatNaturalMin, and combat-utils.getCriticalMultiplier (no criticalMultiplierMin). Canonical rollAttack uses getTargetDefense + resolveCriticalMultiplier. No static caller of rollAutofire/rollFullAttack except a hotfix that wraps rollAutofire; SWSERoll is not a global (macro use unverified). getDefenseValue/resolveTargetContext (:104/:116) and getWeaponDamageFormula (:55) are uncalled locals.
findings.proposedSolution: Delete the two methods and uncalled locals, or make them delegate to rollAttack / FullAttackExecutor (legacy B pending macro check).
findings.regressionTests: Guard: no second getCriticalMultiplier/defense reader in roll entry points.

findings.title: Condition penalty table duplicated 6x; ConditionEngine diverges at step 5
findings.observed: Five tables give helpless (step 5) = 0; ConditionEngine#getConditionPenalty gives -999. Its penalty is consumed only by houserule-condition-track.getTrackPenalties (unreachable-importers-only); live callers use only currentStep/maxStep.
findings.proposedSolution: Export one table from ConditionTrackRules; make readers use derived penalty; drop ConditionEngine table.
findings.regressionTests: Unit test: all readers agree for steps 0-5.

findings.title: combat-ui-behavior-hotfix is a parallel action-execution path (legacy D/F)
findings.observed: Monkey-patches SWSEChat.postRoll; installs a document capture-phase click handler that stopImmediatePropagation()s combat rows to run its own Double/Triple Attack sequence (own full-round spend and rollback) and attack options; applyForcedAttackOption is cloned from combat-feature-handlers; DOM repair/dedupe on every render. FullAttackExecutor already owns double/triple sequencing. Phase-0 doc approves it only as a shrinking bridge.
findings.proposedSolution: Migrate remaining behaviours (multi-attack trigger, option specs, gating) into combat-feature-action-router/FullAttackExecutor, then delete the hotfix and its chat patch.
findings.regressionTests: Double/Triple Attack and Power Attack from sheet produce one spend and same rolls after removal.

findings.proposedSolution: Move presentation modules out of engine/combat; inject dialog callbacks for the services.
